title: Big 12 CFP picture in chaos: BYU, Texas Tech upset losses alter landscape - CBS Sports
description: Two top-10 titans are unbeaten no more in the Big 12
body:
Two top-10 titans are unbeaten no more in the Big 12
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Hold onto your seats, Big 12 fans.Mid-tier teams in the conference spent Saturday taking a sledgehammer to its own playoff argument following UCF's stunning upset of No. 2 BYU in double overtime and Cincinnati's impressive win over previously-unbeaten and No. 8 Texas Tech.Those results have tossed the conference's College Football Playoff hopes in a blender entering Houston-Utah late nearing the end of Week 8.The Bearcats snapped the Red Raiders' nine-game Big 12 winning streak dating back to last season hours before Scott Frost and the Knights held off the Cougars, a week after BYU had beaten Notre Dame to move up to No. 2 in the AP poll. With five top-25 teams entering the weekend, the attention now turns to the primetime battle between the No. 14 Cougars and No. 10 Utah, with the winner getting a leg up on the rest at the top of the conference.
Can either of these teams restore order in the unpredictable league standings?Behind four touchdown passes from JC French and a career-best 173 yards rushing from Cole Tabb, Cincinnati snapped a two-game skid with a signature win and took advantage of Texas Tech's season-long sputters in the passing game. Struggles offensively finally came back to haunt the Red Raiders, who turned it over three times and never recovered from Cincinnati's 21-point surge in the second quarter.The ranked win was only Scott Satterfield's second at Cincinnati in four seasons.
It was personal for the Bearcats, who watched last season's starting quarterback, Brendan Sorsby, leave this offseason via the transfer portal to Texas Tech -- though he never played a down for the Red Raiders. Sorsby was suspended following a gambling investigation before mutually parting ways with Texas Tech in June.Now, Will Hammond and the Red Raiders' offense must likely win out — with Arizona looming among others — to have a chance at repeating as Big 12 champions and securing an automatic berth into the CFP.Top of Big 12 standingsRankTeamOverall RecordConference RecordNo. 10Utah6-03-0No. 2BYU6-13-1No. 8Texas Tech6-13-1No. 14Houston6-13-1No. 25Arizona5-12-1*Houston-Utah play Saturday's late game while Arizona hosts Iowa State.BYU goes down in OrlandoIt's imperative the Big 12's best don't bloody each other up over the second half of the season if this league wants multiple teams in the CFP, especially after BYU's shocking loss at UCF. The selection committee's new conference strength metric helps contextualize league schedules, including disparities between teams with varied schedule difficulty.However, only one of the league's five ranked teams in Week 8 has a strength of schedule ranked inside the top-35 nationally, and that's going to be part of the discussion when the CFP selection committee meets next weekend. Before Saturday's loss, BYU sat No. 1 in strength of record and No. 7 in game control, metrics that will come in handy if Kalani Sitake's team rebounds as the league favorite.Utah has similar numbers, but the Utes' strength of schedule, at No. 99, is the worst in the conference. That changes if Utah moves out of Week 8 as the league's lone unbeaten.Neither BYU nor Texas Tech should be written out of the bracket conversation after one disastrous afternoon, but their cushion got thinner and the conference's margin for error followed.Every CFP contender collecting another loss gives the selection committee another reason to look elsewhere. The Big 12 can sell competitive balance all it wants. Eventually, somebody has to separate.Houston at Utah's significanceSaturday night's late game at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City provides another glimpse into the league title race exiting Week 8, especially if the Utes can stay undefeated against the Cougars. Houston has won four straight games since an early-season loss at Texas Tech and would move into a multi-team tie for second in the conference behind second-ranked BYU with a victory.A Utah win gives the Utes the upper hand in the Big 12 conversation ahead of next week's showdown at Cincinnati before the Nov. 7 showdown with BYU. From Texas Tech's perspective, the best the Red Raiders can finish is 11-1 overall, and from there, the CFP situation gets interesting for Joey McGuire's team.They'll own the head-to-head advantage over Houston in the event the Cougars end up with a single conference loss, but the league goes to tiebreakers with common opponents if Utah or BYU are the teams tied with Texas Tech at the end of the regular season. Cincinnati plays Utah and Houston back-to-back weeks coming up, so the Bearcats will have a say.As you can see, the unpredictable Big 12 and its quest to produce multiple playoff teams this season will be decided over the next few weekends, and the combination of Texas Tech and BYU's losses on Saturday significantly threatens any shot at getting three teams in the final bracket.

        Many viewers of UFC 333 on Saturday were a bit confused when the promotion announced an interim welterweight title fight between Carlos Prates and Michael Morales. The fight, scheduled, for Jan. 30 in Toronto at UFC 336, will pit two young and hungry contenders against one another without the inclusion of full champion Islam Makhachev. According UFC president and CEO Dana White, the intent was for Makhachev to fight on that card. "Islam, on average, fights once a year," White said. "He was slated for January and then said, 'I don't want to fight until after Ramadan.' You can't hold up divisions like this. Backup quarterback Keyone Jenkins accounted for four touchdowns, and the Knights secured their first top-five victory in program history with a goal-line stand in double overtime

        One week after upsetting Notre Dame, No. 2 BYU lost a road thriller 39-31 against UCF in double-overtime. The Knights stopped the Cougars on fourth down to stun BYU and beat their first AP Top 5 team in program history. UCF initially had to settle for a field goal in double-overtime, but a questionable roughing the kicker call turned three points into a first-and-goal from the four-yard line. Quarterback Keyone Jenkins found Utah native Gabe Brousseau four a touchdown and Tyren Hornes on the two-point conversion. BYU went to the air as quarterback Bear Bachmeier was just short on a touchdown to wide receiver Kyle Kasper. They reached second-and-goal from the four-yard line, but Bachmeier threw three incompletions on tough passes to end the game as fans stormed the field. Jenkins, the backup quarterback at UCF, threw for 293 yards, rushed for 35 and scored four touchdowns in a masterful effort. BYU got three touchdowns from quarterback Bear Bachmeier, but UCF's defense stood up at the biggest moment. 
This was the first loss for BYU against an unranked opponent since a 17-13 loss to Kansas on Nov. 16, 2024. Wild end of regulationWith seconds remaining in regulation, BYU appeared to force a strip-sack to reach overtime. The Knights were on the edge of field goal range and would have had a chance to win. Replay review revealed that Knights quarterback Keyone Jenkins was pushing his arm forward with control. Instead of a turnover, it was ruled an incomplete pass with an unsportsmanlike penalty conduct added to the end by BYU captain Keanu Tanuvasa. The penalty pushed the ball into field goal territory for Stone on third down, but Stone's kick was blocked by All-American safety Faletau Satuala. Amazingly, Stone recovered the kick, which appeared to give the Knights a second field goal attempt for the win, but Stone's helmet coming off during the tackle meant there was a mandatory 10-second runoff, ending regulation. 
UCF coach Scott Frost was attempting to set up a second game-winning field goal with a different kicker, but instead the game went into overtime. Poor showingOne week after a historic victory, BYU struggled to maintain the momentum while traveling cross-country. Bachmeier completed only half of his passes and the defense allowed 463 yards. The loss is a significant one as BYU moves to 3-1 in Big 12 play with a heavyweight matchup against No. 10 Utah still on the schedule. This is only the second time in the AP Poll Era that an AP Top 2 team lost against unranked opponents for three straight weeks. 
The only other time? 2007.

title: NC State coaching candidates: Philip Rivers headlines options to replace Dave Doeren - CBS Sports
description: Rivers' son, Gunner, is a top recruit who is committed to NC State in the 2027 recruiting cycle
body:
Rivers' son, Gunner, is a top recruit who is committed to NC State in the 2027 recruiting cycle
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The North Carolina State job is the second Power Four coaching position to come open after the Wolfpack fired longtime coach Dave Doeren on Saturday following a dismal performance in a loss at Stanford on Friday night. Doeren's legacy at NC State stands as one of the program's best coaches, but after going 98-73 in 14 seasons with the Wolfpack, the program decided to make a change. The million-dollar question in Raleigh is who will take over as they look to become a threat in the ACC again. When our CBS Sports insiders began canvassing the landscape for coaching candidates immediately after Doeren was fired, the initial hot list features three current head coaches, three hot coordinators ... and NC State legend Philip Rivers. Philip Rivers, legendary NC State QBRivers would be a fascinating choice given he has no collegiate coaching experience, but after a long career in the NFL, he's been coaching at St. Michael Catholic in Fairhope, Alabama, since 2021. His star player at St. Michael is his son, Gunner, a 4-star quarterback in the 2027 recruiting class who just so happens to be committed to NC State. 
Hiring Rivers would require a leap of faith for the Wolfpack, but when Rivers came out of retirement for the Indianapolis Colts last year, there was plenty of scuttlebutt about his potential as a future NFL coach once his son graduated. Rivers is a well-respected football mind, and it would ensure the Wolfpack kept Gunner Rivers in an NC State uniform. But how he'd fare as a head coach at the collegiate level is a complete mystery. If NC State were to hire Rivers, it'd have to nail down the support system around him to let him focus on football. Running a successful college football program in 2026 requires a unique set of skills, and NC State would need to make a quick, honest assessment of Rivers' strengths and weaknesses and fill those gaps with strong hires around him in terms of personnel, NIL, fundraising and all of the things that go on off the field that contribute to success or failure.Dan Mullen, UNLV coachMullen has insisted he's happy at UNLV and doesn't want to leave Las Vegas, but that won't stop the phone from ringing as he once again has the Rebels among the best in the Group of Six in 2026. NC State could view themselves as much closer to the Mississippi State program Mullen led to prominence rather than the Florida machine that he struggled to mesh with. 
Mullen has had a winning record everywhere he's coached, leading the Bulldogs to a 69-46 record over nine seasons before a 34-15 record at Florida, and he's currently 14-7 at UNLV. The Gators tenure didn't go as hoped, but that job has proven to be tough for anyone to live up to expectations. The real question is whether Mullen is truly as happy as he says in Vegas or if he can't help but wonder if he has one more rebuild in him at a Power Four program. Charles Huff, Memphis coachSpeaking of coaches who win everywhere they go, Huff is in his first season at Memphis and has the Tigers right back in the mix in the American title race at 6-2. Huff has a career 45-27 record at the FBS level since taking over Marshall in 2021 and has never had a losing record in the regular season across three programs. It feels like a matter of time before a Power Four program brings Huff in to see if that trend could continue at the next level, and the 43-year-old has to be under consideration for any program trying to establish a winning culture. Scott Satterfield, Cincinnati coachSatterfield had a rough time in his first stint in the ACC with Louisville, going 25-24 in four seasons with the Cardinals, but he's helped turn things around at Cincinnati and just picked up the biggest win of his tenure in Cincy on Saturday with a big win over No. 8 Texas Tech. Satterfield built his reputation in the state of North Carolina on the west side of the state with Appalachian State, where he went 47-16. If the Wolfpack are looking for someone more established and Mullen isn't the answer, Satterfield could garner a look. 
Glenn Schumann, Georgia DCThe first of a trio of coordinators who could be in the mix for NC State -- and, really, any Power Four job that opens up -- is Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann. The 36-year-old has been with Kirby Smart since he was a student assistant at Alabama starting way back in 2008 and followed Smart to Georgia, where he's worked his way up from linebackers coach to defensive coordinator in Athens. No one is better versed in Smart's vision for program building than Schumann, and after Dan Lanning's success at Oregon, teams might try to pull from the Smart tree again soon. Bryant Haines, Indiana DCHaines has been Curt Cignetti's right-hand man on defense going back to their time at Elon in 2017. While Cignetti has climbed the ladder as arguably the best college coach in the country, Haines has been right alongside, making an impression as one of the best defensive coordinators anywhere. His name popped up on the coaching carousel last year, but Indiana was able to retain him. That's going to get harder and harder every year that Indiana's defense remains dominant. Shannon Dawson, Miami OCDawson is the oldest of the coordinators getting buzz at 49 years old, but his work with the Miami offense, seamlessly transitioning from Cam Ward to Carson Beck to Darian Mensah and finding success, has been particularly notable with how quickly things change in modern college football. This year's Miami offense appears to be his best yet, and the Hurricanes will have to fend off some programs like NC State if they want to keep him on Mario Cristobal's staff beyond 2026.

title: 2026 WNBA Finals: Game 6 location up in the air for Dream vs. Valkyries - CBS Sports
description: The Atlanta Hawks are scheduled to play at State Farm Arena on Thursday night, which leaves the Dream scrambling
body:
The Atlanta Hawks are scheduled to play at State Farm Arena on Thursday night, which leaves the Dream scrambling for an alternative
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Golden State Valkyries held off the Atlanta Dream's comeback attempt on Saturday to secure a 67-62 win in Game 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals. The result evened the series at 2-2 and ensured that the series will return to Atlanta for Game 6 -- though where, specifically, remains to be seen. The location for Game 6 on Thursday is still officially listed as "TBD" on the schedule due to a conflict with State Farm Arena. The Atlanta Hawks, State Farm Arena's primary tenant, are scheduled to host the Cleveland Cavaliers that night. Tip-off for the Hawks game is set for 7 p.m. ET, while tip-off for Game 6 is set for 8 p.m. ET. Obviously, State Farm Arena cannot host two games at the same time, which means one, or both, of the games will have to be adjusted. The WNBA did not have an update to share when reached for comment by CBS Sports. The Dream's primary home is Gateway Center Arena in College Park, which is the league's smallest venue and has a capacity of just 3,500. That is not an ideal setting for a Finals game -- or any playoff game -- and the Dream have played all five of their postseason contests at State Farm Arena. That included Games 3 and 4 of the Finals, which had to be moved due to other conflicts. Game 3 was moved from Oct. 22 to Oct. 21 to avoid a Sombr concert, while Game 4 was moved up to 1 p.m. ET to accommodate the Hawks' home opener against the Houston Rockets on Saturday; the NBA game was shifted back to 8:30 p.m. ET. 
There is less flexibility for both parties moving forward, however, so it's unclear what will happen with Game 6. Here are a few options:Move Game 6 to Wednesday: This is not possible because the Hawks are also at home that night against the Miami Heat.Move Game 6 to Friday: That is not possible because it would create a back-to-back with Game 7, which is set for Saturday in San Francisco, if necessary.Move the Hawks' game: The Hawks also play on Wednesday, but are off on Friday before playing again on Saturday. The Cavaliers, the Hawks' opponent on Thursday, are also off Friday before playing again on Saturday. State Farm Arena has an open date for Friday, so it would be possible to move the Hawks-Cavaliers game to Friday, but that would require multiple NBA franchises, the NBA and broadcast partners to sign off. Play a doubleheader: The Dream and Hawks played a doubleheader at State Farm on Saturday. Could they do it again on Thursday? No. Again, the Hawks play on Wednesday night, so they could not turn around and play on Thursday afternoon. And there's no way WNBA would host Game 6 of the Finals, which will be a potential clincher for one of the two teams, on a Thursday afternoon. Play Game 6 at Gateway Center: This is the easiest solution. It would not be ideal to host Game 6 of the Finals at a 3,500-seat venue, but Gateway Center is the Dream's primary home and there would be no logistical challenges. Play Game 6 at another arena in Atlanta: The Dream could try to move Game 6 to another venue in Atlanta. But where? Gas South Arena holds 13,000, but has a concert scheduled for Thursday. McCamish Pavilion on Georgia Tech's campus -- where the Dream played for two seasons from 2017-18 -- holds 8,600 and has an open date on Thursday. The Georgia State Convocation Center holds 7,500 and appears to have an open date on Thursday as well. Those would be the two best options if the WNBA and the Dream want a bigger crowd, but the Dream haven't played at either venue this season. Would they want to play the biggest game of their season at an unfamiliar venue? After Game 4, Angel Reese made it clear that she hopes the WNBA can find a way to get Game 6 at State Farm Arena. Here's her exchange with a reporter during the postgame press conference:
Question: It took quite a bit to get these Games 3 and 4 moved here, and now that you know you will need a Game 6, what's your hope or expectation of what that would look like coming back to Atlanta?Reese: Just them showing up again. The fan support here has been amazing. We appreciate the love and support and everybody coming out. And being able to force a Game 6 at least. Being able to come here and play in front of the home crowd again would be amazing.Question: Here or Gateway?Reese: HereEarlier this month, the Dream announced a multi-year deal to play all home games at State Farm Arena, starting with the 2027 season, thereby avoiding any such conflicts in the future. Unfortunately for them, that doesn't solve the Game 6 dilemma.

description: A shocking loss to the Cardinal dropped the Wolfpack to 3-4 on the season, ending a 14-year tenure that produced
body:
A shocking loss to the Cardinal dropped the Wolfpack to 3-4 on the season, ending a 14-year tenure that produced 98 wins and 11 bowl trips
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        NC State has fired coach Dave Doeren after 14 seasons, the program announced on Saturday. The news comes one day after the Wolfpack lost 31-28 to Stanford on Friday. "I want to thank Coach Doeren for his service and contributions to NC State, and for always representing the university with pride," NC State athletic director Boo Corrigan said. "I appreciate his leadership during his 14-year tenure and the passion he brought to this role. We wish Dave, Sara and his family the best in the future." The Wolfpack are off to a disappointing 3-4 start in 2026. Outside of an upset victory against Louisville, NC State is 0-4 against Power Four opponents. Against lowly Stanford, NC State allowed 303 yards and four touchdowns to Cardinal quarterback Davis Warren, part of a 477-yard day. Doeren was the model of consistency for most of his tenure, posting 10 winning seasons and 11 bowl appearances in the last 12 seasons. He led NC State to four nine-win seasons, each tied for the second-best mark in program history. 
However, NC State never quite got over the top under Doeren's leadership, leaving the late Chuck Amato's 2002 squad with Philip Rivers as the only 10-win team in school history. And as the NIL era got underway, Doeren struggled to keep the program moving forward. Last season showed promise during an 8-5 season headlined by breakout quarterback CJ Bailey. The Wolfpack invested heavily to retain Bailey, but lost running back Hollywood Smothers (Texas), wide receiver Noah Rogers (Alabama), offensive tackle Jacarrius Peak (South Carolina) and wide receiver Terrell Anderson (USC). 
Now, NC State is set to embark on its first coaching search since 2012. Doeren finishes his tenure with a 98-73 mark and a 52-57 record in ACC play.

title: UFC 333 results, takeaways: Alexander Volkanovski reminds of his greatness - CBS Sports
description: Volkanovski and Yan showed why they might be all-time greats in their respective weight classes on Saturday
body:
Volkanovski and Yan showed why they might be all-time greats in their respective weight classes on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:51 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Following a thrilling fight card and two spectacular title defenses at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi, there is certainly plenty to talk about. Alexander Volkanovski, at 38, passed Brazilian legend Jose Aldo for the most title wins in featherweight history by stopping unbeaten Movsar Evloev in the main event. In the five-round thriller of a co-feature, Petr Yan defended his 135-pound title with a come-from-behind decision win over Merab Dvalishvili in the third meeting between bantamweight legends. Let's take a closer look at the biggest takeaways from what took place inside Etihad Arena. 1. Alexander Volkanovski called his shot and absolutely deliveredAdmittedly, I really didn't know what to make of the 38-year-old living legend's prediction earlier this week when he said that the unbeaten Evloev was a problem for the rest of the division but just not for him and that he would score an early stoppage. Some passed off those words as gamesmanship with Volkanovski hoping to get Evloev off his game or discourage him from wrestling. Not only was the two-time featherweight king true to his words in finishing Evloev inside of two rounds with pinpoint striking, he neutralized just about every aspect of his younger opponent's game in the process. Craig Jones, who was in Volkanovski's corner as a grappling coach, also suggested on social media after the fight that the champion was battling the flu during fight week. Volkanovski, who also equaled Aldo's UFC record for featherweight title defenses (along with owning a 2019 win over him), didn't just cement himself as the greatest 145-pound fighter of all time, he continued to redefine what longevity looks like in the lower weight classes. It's not hyperbole to say that Volkanovski is one of the 10 best fighters in the sport's history. And he's not done yet. 
2. Petr Yan did what likely no other bantamweight could have doneFrom the broken hand Yan entered with in their first meeting in 2023 to the fact that Dvalishivili took their rematch in December on just a two-month turnaround as he ambitiously looked to set the record for title defenses in a calendar year, both fighters entered Saturday's trilogy with legitimate excuses for their defeats. But 10 months after their rematch, with Yan recently healed from back surgery, the third meeting between these legends was a fast-paced and very technical thriller as a rejuvenated Dvalishvili dominated the opening two rounds with his spamming wrestling attack until Yan made the midfight adjustments and used his striking to hurt the former champion down the stretch in a comeback win. Three years after Dvalishvili set a new UFC record for takedown attempts with 49 in their first meeting, he upped that record to an absolutely insane 58 in their trilogy. Every single other bantamweight in the world would've eventually succumbed to Dvalishvili's pressure on this night. He was that dialed in and showcased a variety of new entry points and angles for his takedown attempts. But for the second straight fight, Yan completely took away the superhuman part of Dvalishvili's game that the rest of the division -- throughout the former champion's incredible 14-fight win streak -- were routinely humbled by. Yan's combination of stamina, IQ, toughness and striking technique was legendary on this night as many began to call him, quite possibly, the best bantamweight fighter in history. But it's all part of a larger career comeback story that still isn't getting the attention it deserves as one of the more feel-good developments the sport has produced of late. Yan had both of his young sons by his side on this evening as he entered true living legend status in the sport's history. 
3. Despite solid win, Alexander Volkov likely still in wait-and-see modeFor all of the talk about how much the native of Russia has already done enough to earn a heavyweight title shot yet keeps getting passed over, it's hard not to avoid the feeling that his hard-fought victory over Rizvan Kuniev on Saturday -- on Volkov's 38th birthday -- still might not be enough. To Volkov's credit, he used his post-fight interview to challenge UFC CEO and president Dana White with the same shtick he brought to his surprise cameo at the final press conference just days earlier. Against Kuniev, Volkov did what he always does. He controlled distance, landed the better strikes and avoided allowing his opponent to take over the terms of the fight. And now, with seven wins in his last eight fights (and the only loss being a highly disputed decision in his 2024 rematch with current champion Ciryl Gane), Volkov remains in a great spot within the title hunt. Yet, sadly, he still doesn't feel like a slam dunk choice for the winner of the Gane's first title defense against Josh Hokit next month. Not with superstar Alex Pereira looking to rebound from his loss to Gane at the White House in June by fighting Sergei Pavlovich in December. Credit to Volkov for moving the chains and letting his voice be heard, but his fate still resides in the hands of UFC matchmakers. 4. No need to worry: Lone'er Kavanagh still looks like the future at flyweightFor a 125-pound division that has become the darling of the sport over the past year thanks to the breakout success of 24-year-old champion Joshua Van, it was good to see such a hyped prospect as Kavanagh rebound from a recent stretch of two stoppage defeats in three fights. The 27-year-old native of London was just three months removed from a submission loss to veteran contender Brandon Royval, which heavily muted the momentum he had built to open 2026 when Kavanagh took a short-notice fight at altitude in Mexico City and defeated two-time champion Brandon Moreno. Kavanagh entered quite a stern test in the form of a streaking Ramazan Temirov, the Uzbekistan native who had won his last 12 including all three walks to the Octagon. Kavanagh effectively tamed the aggressive knockout puncher in Temirov and relied upon his speed, defense and technique to expose the more raw and wild parts of his opponent's offensive game. Yet, it was a brutal pair of uppercuts that were most impressive as Kavanagh needed less than one round to make a statement thanks to his fast combination striking that he's still a very serious threat to the flyweight title. 
5. Abdul Rakhman Yakhyaev looks ready (right now) for the top light heavyweightsAt just 25, the native of Russia fits his nickname of "The Hunter" well with an 11-0 career record and 10 finishes. Normally, there wouldn't be much of a need to put the rocket ship on such a young fighter who is 4-0 since making his UFC debut last November. But the combination of the division's glaring lack of depth and the fact that Yakhyaev looks like a finished product already brings the need for an exception. Yakhyaev stepped up considerably in class on Saturday against Nikita Krylov and despite suffering a bloody nose in the early going, he absolutely dominated the battle-tested veteran in all aspects en route to a first-round TKO. Yakhyaev, who recorded the finish with a brutal knee to the head along the cage, called for a top-five opponent next during his post-fight interview. Let's cut to the chase: Yakhyaev is ready.

The usually reliable defense allowed 138 rushing yards to the Buffaloes, the most Colorado has accumulated this season. Since losing on a two-point conversion against Texas Tech, Houston has been a buzzsaw. Quarterback Conner Weigman continued his phenomenal play with nearly 400 total yards and five touchdowns. Amazingly, Houston has won all five historic matchups against Utah, but four came before 1980. The winner of this game has the inside track, and the loser has work to do. Two-quarterback system: Utah is running one of the most fun offensive systems in college football as the Utes are utilizing both Devon Dampier and backup Byrd Ficklin in different sets. Offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven is lining Ficklin up in receiver and running back spots on the field and both running and passing him from those roles to the tune of 6.9 yards per carry. 
Weigman's growth: Houston quarterback Conner Weigman is quietly one of the most improved players in college football. title: Paolo Banchero is hurt again, and this Magic experiment might be cursed - CBS Sports
description: Banchero is reportedly out 4-to-6 weeks with a high ankle sprain
body:
Banchero is reportedly out 4-to-6 weeks with a high ankle sprain
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2024 playoffs were supposed to be the start of something special in Orlando. The Magic had drafted Jalen Suggs, Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero in three straight lotteries and had just pushed Donovan Mitchell and the Cavaliers to seven games. They were young, talented, and when they went all in on the Desmond Bane trade last summer, just about everyone officially stamped them as an Eastern Conference contender. Unfortunately, we've never fully gotten to see what this team could be, and it's starting to look like we never will. Injuries continue to hit them as hard as any team in the NBA. Two games into the 2026-27 season, it's Banchero reportedly headed for a four-to-six week hiatus after suffering a high ankle sprain in Orlando's loss to the Timberwolves on Friday. The Magic just cannot catch a break. Over the last two seasons, the Banchero-Wagner-Suggs trio has managed to play in just 25 games together. Last year, Wagner and Suggs missed a combined 73 games to injury. The year before that, Banchero and Wagner managed just 40 games together. They literally suffered the same injury that year. Banchero tore his oblique in the first week of the season, missed 34 games, and just as he was gearing up to come back, Wagner tore his oblique and missed the next six weeks. 
It's all the more frustrating given the glimpses of actual magic we've seen from this team at full strength. They had the No. 1-seed Pistons down 3-1 in the first round last year until Wagner, of course, missed the last three games of the series with a calf strain and Detroit rallied to win the series. This season, you figured, or hoped, that the needle of injury luck would finally swing in their favor. But here we go again with Banchero, who was off to a roaring start this year with 35 points in the opener and another 14 through the first half on Friday. He was shooting almost 70% from the field. He made three of his four 3-pointers against Atlanta. Aside from the injuries, there have been real questions as to whether Banchero and Wagner can ultimately fit as a duo given both of their shooting inconsistencies. We need to see them together for longer stretches to see if they can make it work, or if Banchero's shooting can improve. The basketball gods just won't let the experiment get off the ground for any real length of time. 
It's too bad, because when Banchero is cooking, he's as lethal a scorer as there is in the league. The Magic can create a lot of inverted mismatches with Banchero's and Wagner's ability to handle the ball and initiate offense at 6-foot-10. Orlando's defense is elite; it had Detroit in a straitjacket for much of that series last year. The pieces are there. But this Banchero injury might seal the fate of this season before it even starts. That sounds premature, but the Magic are already 0-2, and without Banchero for potentially a month and a half, they're very likely going to have to dig out of another deep hole to even think about competing for a playoff spot in the extremely deep East. Truth be told, they were going to have an uphill battle even had they stayed healthy. Now all they can do is hold on as tightly as possible and pray to the basketball gods that nobody else gets hurt before Banchero comes back. The same basketball gods that have seemingly put a curse on a team that might be nearing its end without ever really having had the chance to get started. 
Again, that sounds dramatic. But this feels like a make-or-break year for the Banchero-Wagner duo. The Magic lack the future equity to make another big move. Moving off one of these two is the only real shakeup available. The Magic tried switching coaches, but that's not going to make Banchero or Wagner shoot better and it's not going to make them stay healthy. This was the last shot to really see if this duo can work, and it could not have gotten off to a worse start.

title: UFC 333: Lone'er Kavanagh score beautiful knockout of Ramazan Temirov - CBS Sports
description: Kavanagh showed off his incredible boxing skills to finish off Temirov in thrilling fashion
body:
Kavanagh showed off his incredible boxing skills to finish off Temirov in thrilling fashion

        Lone'er Kavanagh redeemed his flyweight hype.After a recent setback slowed his roll, flyweight contender Lone'er Kavanagh very much looked like a serious player at 125 pounds on Saturday at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi. Kavanagh (11-2), who was submitted by Brandon Royval just three months ago for his second stoppage loss in three fights, bounced back in a major way with a first-round knockout of a dangerous Ramazan Temirov (20-4) in the featured bout inside Etihad Arena. A 27-year-old native of London, Kavanagh has shown flashes of brilliance in five walks to the Octagon entering the Temirov fight, which included a short-notice, five-round decision win at elevation in Mexico City against former champion Brandon Moreno in February that quickly erased the second-round knockout he had suffered against Charles Johnson in his previous fight. Be sure to keep up with all the action on Saturday with our live coverage of UFC 333, including round-by-round scoring and updated fight results throughout the night!
But despite his up-and-down nature of late, Kavanagh put it all together in a systematic breakdown of Temirov, a 29-year-old native of Uzbekistan, who entered having won all three UFC starts while riding a 12-fight win streak overall. Temirov, who knocked out former title challenger Steve Erceg in one round in July, came out head hunting early with his explosive power. But Kavanagh never ran from the danger and relied on his speed, footwork, defense and technique to pick him apart. 
A beautiful left uppercut late in Round 1 rocked Temirov and Kavanagh uncorked a lightning quick combination to floor him. Just as Temirov tried to rise to his feet, Kavanagh met him with another uppercut to drop him into the cage and down again as referee Mike Beltran leaped in to stop the fight at 4:28. 
"I have an amazing team behind me and we work hard, day in and day out, to get these results. We trusted in the plan and we got it done," Kavanagh said. "We learned from previous mistakes and one of those was to keep your hands up. So, I made sure I kept my hands up and I made sure I could counter."Kavanagh, who entered as the No. 6-ranked flyweight in the UFC, didn't hide his intentions for the future after the win."Obviously, I'm here for that belt," Kavanagh said. "Respectfully, anyone can get it. I'm here for that belt."

title: Texas Tech's Big 12 hopes hinge on solving the Brendan Sorsby-sized hole at QB - CBS Sports
description: Two costly turnovers and persistent red-zone struggles from Will Hammond in Saturday's loss to Cincinnati exposed
body:
Two costly turnovers and persistent red-zone struggles from Will Hammond in Saturday's loss to Cincinnati exposed a glaring offensive void after Sorsby's sudden departure
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:26 pm ET

            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Late in the first half against Cincinnati, No. 8 Texas Tech faced a vital moment. The Red Raiders allowed a touchdown to go down 11 points, but had a prime opportunity to erase the lead in an instant. The Red Raiders faced a two-minute drill and would start the second half with the ball. Quarterback Will Hammond dropped back and made a horrendous read, throwing only two yards downfield toward his checkdown, nearly throwing an interception. After two successful run plays that ran the clock down to 31 seconds, Hammond launched a floating jump ball, calmly intercepted by Cincinnati safety MJ Cannon, setting up a touchdown to end the half that made it a three-score game. Cincinnati had this game circled on the calendar after the dramatic Brendan Sorsby saga over the offseason. In a 37-18 loss, a miserable performance for Hammond, the Red Raiders revealed just how much they miss the portal quarterback, who was forced to step away amidst a gambling probe. To turn back the clock, Sorsby played two seasons at Cincinnati, compiling 5,600 yards before entering the transfer portal. Cincinnati sued him over an alleged unpaid buyout. Then he admitted to placing thousands of dollars in bets, resulting in permanent ineligibility from the NCAA. After a dramatic court ruling restored Sorsby's eligibility, outside pressure forced him to step away. 
Without Sorsby, Texas Tech's staff expressed great confidence in Hammond, who is only now one year removed from a torn ACL. But in the miserable loss to Cincinnati, all of the greatest concerns about Hammond came to fruition. 
        
            
                Big 12 College Football Playoff picture thrown into chaos: BYU, Texas Tech upset losses alter landscape
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Hammond's inconsistencyHammond threw for only 227 yards on 37 pass attempts with both an interception and a fumble to boot. The Bearcats scored off both turnovers to build an 18-point halftime lead. During a game-deciding second quarter, Hammond was 2 of 6 for 12 yards with the pick. Cincinnati went on a 21-0 run over the same period. Hammond's inconsistency in the red zone proved especially damaging. He completed only 2 of 6 passes in the red zone, with a sack taken as the Red Raiders failed to score a touchdown on their first three red zone trips. Their first touchdown of the game with less than a minute remaining. 
Through the first three quarters, Hammond had one total completion go for more than 15 yards. More than half of his passing yards -- and only successful shots downfield -- came in the fourth quarter with the game already decided.  And let's be clear, there were plenty of deficiencies shown in the stunning loss. Texas Tech allowed 257 yards on the ground, including a career-high 173 yards to Cincinnati running back Cole Tabb. Last season, the Red Raiders led the Big 12 in rushing defense. The new wave of transfers has not lived up to the standard. Texas Tech's offensive line has also played poorly, despite returning three high-quality starters. They've cycled through three talented running backs, struggling to find a rotation that makes sense. At the same time, opponents are realizing they can stack the box with a quarterback who doesn't scare them. 
There aren't necessarily obvious answers on the roster. Backup Tommy Castellanos started several games in the ACC, but has been embroiled in eligibility cases. He also is an inconsistent passer, completing only 58% of his attempts in his career. Underclassmen Lloyd Jones and Stephen Cannon haven't played much ball. Texas Tech still has a quality win over No. 14 Houston and an important stretch ahead. The Red Raiders host No. 25 Arizona next week before traveling to Oklahoma State in two weeks. The pathway is there for Texas Tech to get back into the Big 12 and College Football Playoff race. Seven games into the season, there is a Brendan Sorsby-shaped hole on the roster. Hammond doesn't look ready to fill it.
